correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed three rooted boundary states A/B/C, base cases h=1,2,3 and period-three cost/count induction. The full-level sets have the predicted size and by exact optimum counts exhaust minimizers. A bottom support vertex with >=2 pendant children is forced into every minimum set; pruning preserves the internal domination constraints. With one surviving child at one bottom parent, the original optimum-to-pruned optimum mapping is exactly 2-to-1 (including h=1). An independent brute-force tree enumerator checked 6 (d,h) regimes, their explicit optimal sets, representative simultaneous prunings, and each single-group sharp case. These finite checks do not establish arbitrary heights.

value.rationale: Minimum optimal-set counts measure placement rigidity in a canonical two-parameter tree family. The sharp change from retaining two pendant leaves to retaining one gives a meaningful, explicit resilience threshold; it is not merely the classical binary case or generic dynamic programming.

checked_sources: Resultary d-ary tree domination semantic query
final_claim: For d>=2,h>=1, gamma is sum_{j=0}^{floor((h-1)/3)}d^(h-1-3j)+1_(3|h); optimum count is d+1 when 3|h else 1. All minimum sets are specified level unions. Deleting terminal leaves while each bottom parent retains at least two leaves preserves all optima; reducing exactly one sibling group to one leaf doubles their count.
limitations: Perfect d-ary trees; terminal deletions only, simultaneous groups below two retained leaves not classified beyond one exceptional group.
